topics.title: Forms of energy and how they change

learn.hook: A fan spins, a bulb glows, a pressure cooker whistles and you run around the playground. All of this needs energy!
points: Energy is what makes things work, move, grow, light up or heat up.
Energy comes in many forms: heat, light, sound, electrical energy and the energy of moving things.
Energy can be stored. Food, fuels like LPG and wood, and batteries all hold stored (chemical) energy.
Energy changes from one form to another. A fan changes electrical energy into movement. A bulb changes electrical energy into light and some heat.
Our body changes the stored energy of food into movement and body heat.

example.q: Priya switches on a torch. Think it through: what energy changes happen?
steps: It changes into electrical energy that flows through the wire.
The bulb changes electrical energy into light (and a little heat).
example.answer: Stored energy in the battery → electrical energy → light.

learn.reallife: Have you noticed that a phone or a laptop gets warm after it has been used for a long time? Some energy always turns into heat!

items.text: Food gives our body ___ to play and work.
A mixer grinder changes electrical energy into ___.

quiz.q: Which of these gives our body energy?
quiz.explain: Food has stored energy. Our body uses it to move, grow and keep warm.
quiz.mistake: Does not know food is our energy source

quiz.q: An electric fan changes electrical energy mainly into
quiz.explain: The fan's blades move. So electrical energy becomes energy of movement.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a fan gives light or cools by making cold

quiz.q: A solar panel changes
quiz.explain: Solar panels catch sunlight and turn it into electricity.
quiz.mistake: Reverses the energy change of a solar panel

quiz.q: Which of these stores energy?
quiz.explain: A battery stores chemical energy that can become electrical energy.
quiz.mistake: Does not know where energy is stored

quiz.q: A loudspeaker changes electrical energy into
quiz.explain: A loudspeaker turns electricity into sound we can hear.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up what different machines produce

quiz.q: When you rub your palms together fast, they get warm. Which form of energy is made?
quiz.explain: Rubbing changes the energy of movement into heat.
quiz.mistake: Does not know movement can turn into heat

quiz.q: What happens to energy in a bulb besides making light?
quiz.explain: A bulb changes most of the electrical energy into light, and some into heat. That is why bulbs get warm.
quiz.mistake: Thinks energy can vanish

quiz.q: Which is an example of energy of movement?
options: A book lying on a shelf
quiz.explain: Anything that moves, like a rolling ball, has energy of movement.
quiz.mistake: Does not know moving things have energy

teach.ask: Gappu taps a torch: 'How does this light up? Where does the energy come from?'
teach.praise: Wow! The battery's stored energy turns into electricity, then into light. Energy is a shape-shifter!
teach.nudge: Where is the energy stored in a torch? What does it change into?

learn.hook: The Sun has been shining for billions of years and gives us light and heat every day for free. What other sources of energy do we use?
points: The Sun is the main source of energy on Earth. Plants use sunlight to make food, and animals eat plants.
Renewable sources do not run out: sunlight, wind, flowing water and biogas.
Non-renewable sources will run out one day: coal, petroleum (from which petrol and diesel are made) and natural gas. They formed deep underground over millions of years.
Burning coal, petrol and diesel makes smoke that pollutes the air.
Biogas is made from cow dung and kitchen waste. Dams use flowing water to make electricity.

example.q: A village has strong sunshine almost all year. Think it through: which source of electricity would suit it best?
steps: Sunlight is free and does not run out.
Solar panels on roofs can turn sunlight into electricity.

learn.reallife: You can see big wind turbines on hills and coasts in Tamil Nadu and Gujarat, and solar panels on many rooftops and railway stations.

games.title: Source check
items: The Sun is the main source of energy on Earth.
Sunlight warms Earth and helps plants make food.
Coal took millions of years to form, so it can run out.
Wind can be used to make electricity.
Wind turns the blades of wind turbines, which make electricity.
Biogas can be made from cow dung.
Cow dung and kitchen waste rot in a tank and give biogas.
Burning petrol keeps the air clean.
Burning petrol gives out smoke and gases that pollute the air.

quiz.q: What is the main source of energy on Earth?
quiz.explain: The Sun gives light and heat. Plants use sunlight to make food, which passes on to animals.
quiz.mistake: Picks a fuel we use instead of the original source

quiz.q: Which of these is a renewable source of energy?
quiz.explain: Wind keeps blowing and will not run out, so it is renewable.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up renewable and non-renewable sources

quiz.q: Which of these is a non-renewable source of energy?
quiz.explain: Coal took millions of years to form underground. Once used up, it cannot be replaced quickly.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all sources are endless

quiz.q: Biogas is made from
quiz.explain: When cow dung and food waste rot inside a closed tank, they give out biogas for cooking.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what biogas is made from

quiz.q: What is a problem with burning coal and petrol?
options: They make smoke that pollutes the air
quiz.explain: Burning these fuels releases smoke and harmful gases into the air.
quiz.mistake: Does not link fuels with air pollution

quiz.q: How do dams help us get electricity?
options: Flowing water turns machines that make electricity
quiz.explain: Water from a dam rushes down and turns turbines, which make electricity.
quiz.mistake: Does not know flowing water can make electricity

quiz.q: Solar panels get their energy from
quiz.explain: Solar panels change sunlight into electricity.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up solar with other sources

quiz.q: Why should we use more renewable energy?
options: It will not run out and causes less pollution
quiz.explain: Renewable sources like sun and wind last forever and make little or no smoke.
quiz.mistake: Does not see the benefit of renewable sources

teach.ask: Gappu looks at a windmill: 'Will wind run out like petrol? Which sources of energy last forever?'
teach.praise: Got it! Sun and wind are renewable and clean; coal and petrol will run out and make smoke.
teach.nudge: Which sources will run out one day, and which never will?

learn.hook: If every home in India switched off just one extra light for an hour each day, a huge amount of electricity would be saved!
points: Switch off lights, fans and TVs when you leave a room.
LED bulbs give good light but use much less electricity than old bulbs.
When buying a fridge or AC, look for the star label. More stars means it uses less electricity.
Use sunlight during the day: open the curtains instead of switching on lights.
Walk, cycle or use buses and trains for short trips. Cover pots while cooking and use a pressure cooker to save gas.

example.q: An old bulb uses 60 watts. An LED bulb gives the same light using 10 watts. How many watts does the LED save?

learn.reallife: 14 December is National Energy Conservation Day in India. Make a 'Switch-off Squad' in your class to check lights and fans at break time!

games.title: Saver or waster?
items: Switching off the fan when leaving
Leaving the TV on with nobody watching
Lights on in an empty room

items.q: Bulb that uses the least electricity
Label that shows how well an appliance saves power
Ride this for a short trip instead of a car

quiz.q: Which bulb uses the least electricity for the same light?
options: A bulb left on all night
quiz.explain: LED bulbs give the same light with much less electricity.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all bulbs use the same power

quiz.q: An old bulb uses 60 watts and an LED bulb uses 10 watts. How many fewer watts does the LED use?
quiz.explain: 60 − 10 = 50. So the LED uses 50 watts less.
quiz.mistake: Adds the numbers or divides instead of subtracting

quiz.q: Two fridges of the same size: one has 5 stars on its label and one has 2 stars. Which uses less electricity?
quiz.explain: More stars on the energy label means the appliance uses less electricity.
quiz.mistake: Thinks stars mean the price or size

quiz.q: What should you do when you leave your room?
options: Switch off the lights and fan
quiz.explain: Switching off saves electricity when nobody is using the room.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that machines use energy even when no one is there

quiz.q: How does covering a pot while cooking help?
options: Food cooks faster and less gas is used
quiz.explain: A lid keeps the heat inside, so food cooks faster with less fuel.
quiz.mistake: Does not know heat escapes from an open pot

quiz.q: Which way of going to a nearby shop saves fuel?
options: Taking a motorbike for two minutes
quiz.explain: Walking and cycling use no fuel and keep us fit too.
quiz.mistake: Thinks short car trips do not use fuel

quiz.q: In the daytime, the best way to light up a classroom is to
options: close all the windows and switch on lights
open the windows and curtains to let sunlight in
quiz.explain: Sunlight is free light. Using it saves electricity.
quiz.mistake: Forgets about using natural light

quiz.q: National Energy Conservation Day in India is on
quiz.explain: India marks National Energy Conservation Day on 14 December to remind everyone to save energy.
quiz.mistake: Mixes it up with World Water Day or World Environment Day

teach.ask: Gappu sees lights on in an empty room: 'Is that a waste? How can my family save energy?'
teach.praise: Yes! Switch off, use LED bulbs, use sunlight and cycle. My family is now an energy-saving team!
teach.nudge: What should we do with lights and fans when we leave? Which kind of bulb saves electricity?
